book.aeroscapes_reimagine.field_guide.we: How to get started, what changes in survival, and how to use the guide.
The Overworld is an archipelago in the sky. Set up a home island with water, food, and supplies. Plan the way back before you cross a gap. A lower island is often easier to reach than to leave.

Watch thirst and temperature. Carry [purified water](entry://island/clean_water) and varied food. A poor diet weakens attacks. Right-click loose items or sneak near them to pick them up. Many raw materials are picked up automatically.

Start [stone tools](entry://island/rock) by striking stone with flint. Work the loose stones with one in each hand. Making iron and better gear needs Smithing talents. Found tools can be used at their normal harvest tier.

Your starting class gives you a first talent. Practice earns points to spend in the Talents screen. Advanced tools and weapons work more slowly until trained, and untrained armor gives much less protection.

Bridges work for short crossings. A hook helps on cliffs, and a glider uses stamina to control descent. For longer trips, build an airship or [look for a stranded ship](entry://flight/wreck_search) to restore.

Open any step to read it. Doing the action records progress and gives no rewards. Start with [Your starting island](category://island), find recipes in EMI, and use Ponder to see how Create machines fit together.
book.aeroscapes_reimagine.field_guide.is: Gather your first log
Find a tree away from the edge and break one log by hand. The map opens a new step as you finish each action. You can use equipment you find, take side routes, or skip the guide entirely.
Saw planks
Put a log in your inventory crafting grid and take the planks.
Make handles
Put two planks one above the other in the inventory grid to make sticks. Save some for later tool heads.
Place a crafting table
Fill the four slots in your inventory crafting grid with planks, then place the crafting table on the ground.
Make a wooden pickaxe
At the table, put three planks across the top row and two sticks down the middle. Take the pickaxe.
Mine cobblestone
Mine ordinary gray stone with the wooden pickaxe. Keep eight cobblestone for a furnace.
Find gravel and get flint
Look for loose gray gravel on slopes and near water. Break several blocks by hand or with a shovel until flint drops. Leave yourself solid ground to stand on.
Strike stones loose

Break gravel for flint, then right-click plain stone with it. A successful strike drops a loose stone and leaves cobblestone behind. If the flint breaks, try another piece. Gather two loose stones to shape your first pickaxe head.
Collect a second rock
Strike another block of plain stone until you have two rocks. Extra rocks let you make more tool heads.
Put a rock in each hand
Split the stack. Put one rock on the hotbar and one in your off-hand slot beside the armor slots. Select the hotbar rock.
Knap a pickaxe head
Hold a loose stone in each hand and right-click the air. Leave one full row in the 3×3 grid to shape a pickaxe head. Click a cell again to restore it. Take the pickaxe head from the result slot.
Fit the stone head
Fit the head to a stick in any two crafting slots. This pick gets you to copper, the metal for your first forge. If you find a tool that can mine copper, you can head straight for the ore.
Mine coal
Use the stone pickaxe on coal ore, marked by black flecks. Save some coal for the furnace, torches and later machinery.
Place a furnace
Put eight cobblestone around the center of the crafting table grid. Place the furnace beside the workbench.
Light your campsite
Put coal above a stick to make torches. Light an enclosed area with a roof and a way to close the entrance. Place a torch inside before dark.
Knap other stone tools
Shape axe, shovel and hoe heads in the same two-stone grid. Look up the shapes in EMI and fit each head to a stick. Start with an axe if you need lumber to turn your camp into a base.
Make a stone shovel
Knap a single cell in the middle column. Fit the shovel head to a stick for faster sand and gravel digging.
Make a stone hoe
Knap two touching cells in one row. Fit the hoe head to a stick so you can till a seed bed.
Gather wheat seeds
Break short grass in the open until wheat seeds drop. Look for dirt near a water source before planting.
Sow wheat
Right-click dirt with the hoe, then right-click the farmland with seeds. Plant in a season and place where the crop can grow.
Harvest ripe wheat
Wait for the crop to turn golden, then harvest it and replant. Use Jade to check the growth stage when in doubt.
Bake bread
Place three wheat in a row on the crafting table. Browse Farmer’s Delight in EMI when you want to turn your harvest into other meals.
Gather sand for bottles
Find sand near water. Gather at least three blocks for a batch of glass bottles.
Smelt glass
Smelt sand in the furnace. Wait for three glass blocks so you can make a set of bottles.
Craft bottles
At the workbench, place three glass in a V: left and right on one row, center on the row below.
Purify drinking water
Before following an ore vein away from camp, fill a bottle by right-clicking a water source. Heat the filled bottle in a furnace and take the purified water with you.
Store a reserve at home
Surround the center of the crafting grid with planks. Put the chest inside the lit shelter and leave some wood, food and spare tools there.
Make a bed
Put three wool of the same color above three planks. Set the bed in your shelter. If you have no sheep, look for wool in structures or make it from string.
Spend a night at home
Right-click the bed after dark to sleep and set your return point. Keep the entrance lit and clear.
book.aeroscapes_reimagine.field_guide.wo: Continue the route from the previous chapter.
Mine raw copper
Take your stone pickaxe to copper ore, speckled with orange and green. Mine several blocks for a hammer and a pickaxe head.
Start working copper
Start your forge with the copper your stone pick can mine. Smelt the raw copper and set aside ingots for a hammer and a pickaxe head. That copper pick will open up iron ore.
Build a smithing hammer
Make the hammer that will turn a block of stone into your first anvil. On a crafting table, put copper ingots in the top-middle and middle-right, with sticks in the center and bottom-left.
Set up a forge
Pick a spot near the furnace for the stone smithing anvil. Crouch and right-click plain stone with your smithing hammer. Leave room in front of the anvil so you can work there.
Make wooden tongs
Wooden tongs let you carry hot metal from the furnace to the anvil. Make them from sticks and equip them in your off hand.
Heat three copper ingots
Put three copper ingots back in the furnace to heat them for forging. With tongs in your off hand, take the hot ingots straight to the anvil.
Forge a copper head

Line up three hot copper ingots on the stone anvil. Close the menu and crouch and right-click with the hammer. Stand up and strike three times as the marker reaches the target. Take the head with tongs equipped.
Cool the copper head
The head needs to cool before you fit it to a handle. Drop it in water, wait for steam and pick it up. If it cooled on its own, it is ready to use.
Finish the copper pick
Place the cooled head above a stick in the crafting grid. Take your new pick to an iron vein and bring back enough ore to keep the forge going.
Mine iron ore
Look for beige-flecked iron ore and break it with the copper pickaxe. Collect enough for a blast furnace, a pickaxe head and workshop parts.
Start working iron

Mine iron ore with your copper pick and smelt what you bring back. Set aside ingots for a pick that can mine zinc and a bucket that can bring water to the workshop. You'll need the smithing talent to forge the pick.
Learn iron toolmaking
Making stone or copper gear by hand counts as Smithing practice. Use your first point in Talents → Professions → Smithing to learn Iron Work Tools and put your new iron to work.
Prepare smooth stone
Smelt cobblestone into stone, then smelt the stone a second time. You need three smooth stone blocks for the blast furnace.
Heat iron for forging

A blast furnace brings iron up to forging temperature. Load raw iron or ingots and take the hot metal with tongs in your off hand. Check the item tooltip for its temperature before you take it to the anvil.
Heat three iron ingots
For the pickaxe head, heat raw iron or ingots in the blast furnace. Take three hot ingots straight to the anvil with your tongs ready.
Forge an iron head
Set three hot ingots side by side in a row. Close the menu, crouch and right-click with the hammer. Stand and time three blows. Retrieve the iron head with tongs equipped.
Cool the iron head
Drop the hot head in water and pick it up when it cools. Keep water near the anvil so the next tool can go straight from forging to cooling.
Finish the iron pick
Fit the cooled head to a stick. With this pick you can bring home zinc for brass and redstone for the first ship. If you want to keep smithing, follow the steel and diamond branch.
Mine zinc
Use your iron pickaxe on Create’s pale green zinc ore. Save the zinc for brass.
Mine redstone
Mine redstone ore with the iron pickaxe. Save the dust for controls and later wiring.
Forge a bucket
Make a bucket to bring a stream to your first water wheel. Set three cold iron ingots in a V on the stone anvil. Close the menu, stand and right-click three times with the hammer. Take the bucket.
Collect water for power
Right-click a water source with your bucket. Bring it to the workshop to drive a water wheel.
Make andesite alloy
Andesite alloy goes into the shafts and machines that will carry power around your workshop. Make a batch from two andesite and two iron nuggets in a checkerboard pattern.
Make shafts
Craft shafts from two andesite alloy stacked vertically. A shaft passes rotation along its axis.
Make an andesite casing
Strip a placed log with an axe and right-click the stripped log with andesite alloy. Break the casing to collect it.
Start a water drive
Turn a stream into power for the workshop. Surround a shaft with planks on the crafting table. Set the wheel with its axle pointing toward the work area and let water flow beneath it.
Set up the press
Put the water wheel to work with a press made from a shaft, andesite casing and iron block. Connect its shaft to the wheel and leave one block of air above the work surface.
Press iron sheets
Put an iron ingot on a depot or drop it under the powered press. After the press strikes, collect the sheet. Press a batch while the drive is running. Your saw and burner both need sheets.
Build a saw and gears
Build the saw from three sheets, an iron ingot and an andesite casing. It will work with the press to make the engine. Leave room for the drive and check the saw's input face in Ponder.
Make small cogwheels
Make small cogwheels from shafts and planks. Pair them with large ones to get more speed from the water wheel for your mixer.
Make large cogwheels
Make at least two large cogwheels. Each large cog driving a small one doubles its speed. Repeat on another shaft to turn the wheel's 8 RPM into 32 RPM for the mixer.
Place a basin
Make a basin from five pieces of andesite alloy. This is where copper and zinc will become brass. Leave room for a burner below the basin and a mixer two blocks above.
Set up a mixer
Make the mixer from a whisk, cogwheel and andesite casing. Mount it with one air block above the basin. Use Ponder to route the geared drive into the mixer from above.
Reach the Nether

Head to the Nether for a heat source for your basin. An iron pickaxe is enough if you repair a ruined portal or cast the frame with water and lava. Check ruin chests for flint and steel or a fire charge.
If you need to craft flint and steel, use flint and a cold steel ingot from the steel branch. Put on one piece of gold armor before you step through the portal.
Collect netherrack
Mine a piece of netherrack for the burner housing. Mark the way back while the portal is still close. You'll want a clear route out once you have a blaze.
Craft an empty Blaze Burner
Surround a piece of netherrack on four sides with iron sheets. Take the empty Blaze Burner back to the Nether and find a fortress where you can fill it.
Capture a blaze
Right-click a blaze with the empty burner to capture it. Bring the filled burner home and set it directly below the basin to heat the brass mix.
Smelt zinc ingots
Smelt raw zinc. Bring zinc and copper ingots to the basin, with coal for the burner.
Mix brass
Mine zinc with an iron pick and smelt it. Spin the mixer at 32 RPM or faster. Right-click the blaze burner with coal, then put the copper and zinc ingots into the heated basin.
Make a brass casing
Turn your first brass into a casing for the ship's lift control. Strip a log with an axe, right-click it with a brass ingot and mine the casing.
Set up a reforging anvil
At an ordinary anvil, open the Reforging tab. Bring a fully repaired tool or piece of armor whose current quality you are ready to give up.
Reforge equipment
Check EMI for the material your gear takes. Put it on the left, the gear in the middle and lapis on the right. Reforging replaces the old quality immediately. The new one can be worse.
Place an enchanting table
Take four obsidian you found or mined with steel or better, two diamonds and a book to the crafting table. Place the enchanting table with room for chiseled bookshelves two blocks away.
Build an enchantment library

Place the enchanted books you want in chiseled shelves two blocks from the table, level with it or up to three blocks higher. Ordinary books give basic enchantments up to II. Ancient books from major dungeons list their own limit. Learn the matching talent to apply the enchantment.
Place an alloy furnace
Steel starts with a furnace of its own. Surround a blast furnace with eight brick blocks on the crafting table. Set up the alloy furnace in your workshop to turn iron and coal into crude steel.
Smelt crude steel
Follow the Overgeared recipe in EMI. Feed three iron ingots and one coal into the alloy furnace and take the crude steel. You'll refine it into an ingot at the anvil.
Reheat the crude steel
Reheat the crude steel in the blast furnace. Have your tongs ready to take it straight to the anvil while it is still hot enough to work.
Set up an iron smithing anvil
Set up an iron smithing anvil to work steel. Crouch and right-click an ordinary iron anvil with the smithing hammer to convert it.
Refine crude steel
Work one hot piece of crude steel at a time on the iron smithing anvil. Three ordinary hammer hits turn it into a hot steel ingot. Make three ingots for the pickaxe head.
Learn steel toolmaking
Keep practicing Smithing after iron to learn Steel Work Tools. For each recipe, check the required anvil and hammer in EMI.
Forge a steel pickaxe head
Line up three hot steel ingots on the iron smithing anvil. Start forging and time four strikes. Take the head with tongs and cool it before fitting the handle.
Cool the steel head
Drop the hot steel head in water. Once it has cooled, pick it up for the handle.
Forge a steel pick
Put the cooled head above a stick. Your steel pick opens up obsidian for projects such as an enchanting workshop. Keep the pick if you plan to upgrade it with a diamond.
Obtain a diamond
Look for diamond ore deep in the larger islands and use an iron pickaxe or better. A diamond from a chest also works.
Find a diamond template
Take your search for a diamond upgrade template to mineshafts, buried treasure or pillager outposts. Once you have one, you can copy it. You can also learn to forge the template in the Smithing tree.
Learn Diamond Work Tools
Continue the work tools branch of Smithing after steel. Learn the diamond talent to use the upgrade at a smithing table.
Upgrade to diamond
At a smithing table, combine a diamond upgrade template, a steel pickaxe and one diamond. A pickaxe found on an expedition already mines at diamond tier. Its Mining talent brings it up to full speed.
book.aeroscapes_reimagine.field_guide.fl: Continue the route from the previous chapter.
Process an engine assembly

Your workshop saw and press can make the engine's core. Open the sequence in EMI, then run an iron sheet through the powered saw and press in that order for eight cycles. Keep spare sheets in case you get scrap.
Make a portable engine
Stack an iron sheet, the engine assembly and a blast furnace from top to bottom. Save coal so this engine can keep your propeller turning after you leave the dock.
Craft envelope blocks

Plan the balloon around the air inside it. A 3×3×3 shell holds only one air block, so build a bigger chamber over a light deck. The recipe shows white wool as an example. Use the same arrangement with wool of another color.
Craft an adjustable burner
An Adjustable Burner puts hot air into the envelope. Use its Ponder scene to see which way it faces and where the redstone signal goes.
Prepare the lift system
Put a stick above the brass casing you made in the workshop. The lever changes the burner signal in steps so you can adjust lift from the deck.
Make a propeller bearing
Use a Propeller Bearing to turn the engine’s rotation into forward thrust. Mount the bearing with its moving face away from the hull.
Build a propeller
Make at least two sails for blades. For a white sail, put wool and a stick in the top row, then a stick and andesite alloy below. Leave both sides of the blades clear so they can sweep freely.
Place a stonecutter
Craft a stonecutter from an iron ingot and three stone blocks. It gives you a direct way to make industrial iron.
Cut industrial iron
Cut an iron ingot in a stonecutter and select industrial iron blocks. Set one aside for the swivel bearing that will turn the steering assembly.
Craft a swivel bearing
Stack a slab, an industrial iron block and a cogwheel. The swivel bearing lets the steering assembly turn independently of the deck.
Prepare the steering
Put the helm where you can steer from the deck. Its Ponder scene shows how shafts carry its motion to the swivel bearing.
Make Super Glue
Use Super Glue to join the deck and fixed equipment into one body. Give each part that needs to rotate its own glued section.
Prepare ship assembly
The Physics Assembler lets the finished hull move as one body. Watch its Ponder scene before you release the build from the dock.
Begin the balloon shell
Start from solid ground. Build a light deck and enclose a hollow chamber with envelope blocks. Leave an opening for the burner to feed hot air straight into the chamber.
Mount the burner
Set the burner in the bottom of the balloon with its outlet facing the cavity. Check the seal around it and the rest of the shell so the hot air stays inside.
Install the lift system
Place the throttle within reach on the deck and wire its redstone output to the burner. Keep the signal low while you finish assembling the ship.
Install the engine
Mount the portable engine with its shaft facing the propeller drive. Leave the fuel opening accessible from the hull. Add coal and check that the output shaft turns.
Test the propeller
Connect the engine to the bearing and attach at least two sails. Check that the blades spin clear of the hull and push forward. If thrust points aft, use a wrench or reverse the drive.
Assemble the swivel mount
Mount the steering assembly on the swivel bearing as a separate moving section. Use Ponder to connect the drive to the bearing's input so the whole section can turn.
Test the helm
Hold right-click on the steering wheel and move the mouse. Make sure the steering assembly can turn both ways without touching the deck before you release the hull.
Release the hull
Glue the hull and fixed machinery into one body. Keep the dock and rotating sections separate. Use the Physics Assembler on the glued hull, pull its lever and step aboard the released ship.
Fill the balloon
Set the burner's maximum output on its panel, then raise the throttle to send hot air into the sealed chamber. If fill never rises, look for a gap or check that the burner faces inside.
Check the lift
In Controls, find the Aeroscapes Reimagine flight section. Assign Open preflight information. Open it on deck and refresh to check fuel, fill and whether balloon support covers the hull's mass.
Take off
Raise the throttle a little at a time until you lift. Use the propeller and helm to move a few blocks from the dock. Stay over the island, clear of its edge, and turn back while home is close.
Land the ship
Ease off thrust and approach level ground slowly. Lower lift in small steps and come to a stop on a clear spot before unloading. When you expand the ship or workshop, use Ponder and EMI.
Provision an expedition
Once you can leave the dock and land again, pack for a trip between islands. Take purified water, food and fuel for the way back. A grappling hook helps you climb cliffs and get back aboard.
Find a stranded ship

Search around ruins and landing sites for stranded or tethered ships. Bring blocks for a safe approach and shears for the tether. Use what you find for a new build or put the old hull back in the air.
Salvage fittings
If you want to build your own hull, take any working propeller bearing, burner or steering wheel you find. Use those parts when you reach the corresponding steps of the build.
Inspect the wreck
Start by reconnecting the drive. Fit a shaft in the gap between the deck gearbox and the shaft leading aft. Align it with the rest of the drive.
Check the envelope and wire the throttle to the burner. Test the steering and add a swivel bearing if needed. Get a Physics Assembler before you release the hull.
Make a wreck flyable
Glue the deck and fixed equipment together. Keep the propeller blades in a separate assembly so they still turn. Release the mooring rope before you detach the ship.
Right-click the rope connector or shore winch with shears. Use the assembler, then board the freed ship near the wreck site. Check the balloon and test the flight before heading farther.
Gather ship fittings
Start with what will lift and drive the new hull. Gather envelope blocks, an adjustable burner, a throttle lever, a portable engine, a propeller bearing and two matching sails.
Add a steering wheel, swivel bearing, Super Glue and a Physics Assembler. Find missing parts on other hulls or make them using EMI. Once the fittings are ready, start the shell.
book.aeroscapes_reimagine.field_guide.is: Strike stone with flint to gather the two pieces for your first pickaxe head.
Open the knapping grid with a stone in each hand and shape the pickaxe head.
Fit the head to a handle and start mining copper for your first forge.
Heat a bottle of water from a source so you can take clean water on the trail.
Use the same knapping grid for an axe, shovel or hoe to equip your camp.
book.aeroscapes_reimagine.field_guide.wo: Smelt copper for your first forge. A copper pickaxe leads to iron.
Make a copper hammer, turn stone into an anvil and get tongs ready for hot metal.
Heat three ingots and time three blows to forge the pickaxe head that gets you to iron.
Cool the copper head in water and fit it to a stick. Take the pick to an iron vein.
Smelt the iron your copper pick unlocks. Save enough for a pickaxe and a bucket.
Practice on stone or copper equipment to earn the talent for forging iron tools.
Heat iron to forging temperature in a blast furnace and carry it with tongs.
Take three hot iron ingots to the anvil and time three strikes for a pickaxe head.
Cool the forged head and fit it to a stick. Bring back zinc and redstone for the ship.
Use lapis and the material listed in EMI to roll a new quality for your gear.
Stock chiseled shelves with the books for the enchantments you want to apply.
Build an alloy furnace to turn iron and coal into crude steel.
Work hot crude steel on an iron smithing anvil to make ingots for a pickaxe head.
Build on iron toolmaking and learn the talent that lets you forge steel tools.
Forge a pick from three hot steel ingots and use it to mine obsidian.
Search mineshafts, buried treasure or pillager outposts for the template to upgrade your steel pick.
Learn diamond toolmaking and upgrade the steel pick at a smithing table.
Forge a bucket from three cold iron ingots to bring water to the workshop.
Bring water to the wheel and make your first Create drive.
Use the water drive to press iron sheets for the saw and burner.
Build the saw for the engine and use cogwheels to speed up the mixer.
Bring the geared drive to the mixer and leave room below the basin for heat.
Restore a ruined portal or cast a frame to reach the Nether for a blaze.
Capture a blaze in an empty burner to heat the basin for brass.
Mix copper and zinc with heat and make a brass casing for the ship's lift control.
book.aeroscapes_reimagine.field_guide.fl: Put the workshop saw and press to work on the core of your ship's engine.
Make the envelope, burner and lever so you can adjust lift from the deck.
Fit at least two sails to a propeller bearing to turn rotation into forward thrust.
Link the helm to a swivel bearing so you can steer from the deck.
Prepare the glue and assembler that will free the finished hull from the dock.
Look around ruins and landing sites for a ship you can salvage or restore.
Gather working parts from a wreck and use them to build a hull of your own.
Restore the drive on a moored ship and free the hull for a flight test.
Seal the balloon over a light deck and connect its burner to the throttle.
Fuel the engine and check that the propeller turns freely and pushes forward.
Link the helm to the swivel and test both turns before leaving the dock.
Glue the fixed parts together and use the assembler to free the hull from the dock.
Fill the balloon with hot air and check that it can support the hull's mass.
Lift off a little at a time and turn back while you are close to the dock.
Slow down and lower lift in steps to set the ship down on clear ground.
Pack purified water, food and fuel for the flight to the next island and back.
